summary.headline: Rajputana Stainless Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to INR360 crore and PAT 79% to INR23.7 crore, with operating cash flow weak at INR4.5 crore in H1.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew about 33% YoY to INR360 crore, with operating EBITDA up 38% to INR33.4 crore (9.3% margin) and PAT up 79% to INR23.7 crore. H1 revenue was INR666 crore and H1 PAT INR43.9 crore, up 80%, and management said H1 PAT was about 88% of FY26 full-year PAT. The company is debt-free after IPO proceeds were used to repay debt, and capacity utilisation is reported at over 99%. Cash conversion weakened, with H1 operating cash flow of about INR4.5 crore, mainly absorbed by receivables as the company shifted from trader channels to direct end-user sales with 60-90 day terms.

financial_highlights.value: INR232-242 crore (figure quoted inconsistently in call)

financial_highlights.change: debtor days said to be up 3-4 days

financial_highlights.metric: Order book at start of H2
financial_highlights.value: about INR500 crore, including over INR80 crore aerospace and defence

segments.name: Aerospace and defence
segments.commentary: Over INR80 crore of the INR500 crore order book; company recently aerospace-certified and has begun supplying defence companies abroad. Management said quantities were broadly flat but higher-grade mix lifted revenue and profit, and does not track exact revenue share.

segments.name: Seamless pipes (new vertical)
segments.commentary: Planned entry into seamless pipe production with a B2B bar product to supply seamless pipe makers; the INR18.57 crore IPO-funded allocation is still unutilised. Management cited a seamless-pipe industry size of about 2.1 lakh tonnes/year growing about 15% a year, with plants at about 85% utilisation.

segments.name: Bright bar
segments.commentary: Bright bar capacity of 6,000 tonnes is about 60% utilised, per management.

segments.name: Melt and rolling
segments.commentary: Billet (melting) utilisation at 99% and rolled products at 99.45% in Q2; company describes itself as running at full capacity.

guidance_outlook: Melting capacity to rise from 48,000 tonnes to 60,000 tonnes, with commissioning expected in Q4 FY27 (calendar 2026-27 Q4 as stated).
Solar captive plants expected to start by end of calendar 2026, with power cost savings from 1 January 2027; windmill production targeted for end-March (2027).
Capacity expansion to be funded by internal accruals; management said no additional working capital is needed until about 60,000 tonnes, when some may be required.
Management expects free cash flow to be positive for the full year.
Long-term vision of about 2 lakh tonnes of capacity by 2031, described as 4-5 years away.
Management expects a positive EBITDA margin trend over the next three to four quarters.
Seamless pipe unit reported target of 80% utilisation in its first year; management said it has soft inquiries but no firm commitments were stated.
capex_capacity: Current capacity 48,000 tonnes melting, 36,000 tonnes rolling and 6,000 tonnes bright bar; over 80 grades and 5,000+ SKUs.
Expansion from 48,000 to 60,000 tonnes melting targeted for Q4 FY27, about a 25% increase, funded by internal accruals.
Seamless pipe vertical: INR18.57 crore of IPO proceeds still unused as of 30 September; delay attributed to sourcing the latest machinery intended to last 25-30 years.
Solar plants to cover captive power needs from 1 January 2027; windmill production targeted for end-March; power is about 80% of power cost covered by these projects.
Management said it is reconsidering the seamless machine order to a higher-end unit with greater output.
demand_pricing: Order-based (make-to-order) model with raw material hedged against each order; scrap sourcing about 39% imported, with management saying Indian buyers are favoured as the world exports scrap to India.
Consumables not hedged, estimated at about 10-12% of raw material cost; management said gross profit rose about 22% in Q2 despite higher other costs.
Management said prices are customer-specific and not standardised, supporting margins.
Demand drivers cited: AI-related machinery fasteners/components (mainly US demand), oil and gas repair work, and defence and aerospace.
Management said there is a large inquiry pipeline for seamless pipes from the Middle East, Europe and US, but did not quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: What were Q2 production and capacity utilisation figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation was over 99% and continuous for two years: billets 99%, rolled products 99.45%, bright bar about 60%. Revenue growth was attributed to a richer specialty grade mix rather than volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H1 operating cash flow only about INR4.5 crore against PAT of INR43.9 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash went into working capital, mainly receivables, as the company shifted from trader channels to direct end-users such as BHEL and L&T, who pay on 60-90 day terms. Debtor days were said to be up only 3-4 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle and how much more working capital will growth need?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable cycle about 52 days; payables said to be under 10 days (not certain). Expansion to 60,000 tonnes to be funded by internal accruals, with working capital needs possible only beyond that level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and why is the IPO money for the seamless pipe plant still unspent?
qa_highlights.answer: Two verticals: capacity expansion to 60,000 tonnes and a consumer-facing seamless pipe entry. Management said INR18.57 crore is unused for the seamless plant because it is waiting for the latest machinery, and about INR4 crore of other IPO funds is also unused.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR34.5 crore loan and advance a related-party transaction?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vishal Vijayvargiya said it is not a related-party loan but an inter-corporate deposit that carries interest.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall YoY despite raw material hedging?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only consumables (about 10-12% of raw material cost) cannot be hedged; other costs grew faster than sales, which kept EBITDA margin gains small (9.0% to 9.3%).

qa_highlights.question: What is the import share of scrap, and are there logistics issues?
qa_highlights.answer: About 39% of scrap is imported. Management said there have been delays, but ongoing contracts with dealers have avoided disruption, and transit costs have been absorbed by scrap sellers.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the seamless pipe market and what are the entry barriers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated industry size at about 2.1 lakh tonnes/year growing about 15% a year, with plants at about 85% utilisation. It said technical know-how and metallurgy are the main entry barriers, and that the company's scrap-to-finished-pipe integration is an advantage.

risks_watch: Cash conversion: H1 operating cash flow of about INR4.5 crore against PAT of INR43.9 crore; receivables rising with direct end-user sales on 60-90 day terms.
Commissioning risk on the 48,000 to 60,000 tonne expansion (Q4 FY27) and the solar and windmill projects (targeted end-2026 and end-March).
The INR18.57 crore seamless-pipe allocation is unspent and timing has slipped; the target of 80% utilisation in year one is unsupported by disclosed commitments.
Gross margin decline YoY despite hedging; cost growth above sales growth.
Management did not quantify aerospace and defence revenue share; figures for receivables were quoted inconsistently (INR232 crore vs INR242 crore).
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, demand and the seamless pipe opportunity, with frequent use of superlatives. More cautious on cash conversion and capex timing, where answers were partial and some figures were corrected on the call.
key_quotes: So we are not in the race of producing more. We are in the race of producing the right product for the right customer at the right price.
We have taken the route of directly going to the end-user base, which has ensured that our receivable timings have increased

adds.what: Melting capacity expansion from 48,000 t to 60,000 t/yr
Seamless pipe vertical (new B2B bar product line), planned; INR18.57 crore IPO allocation unutilised

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance; management guides melting capacity rising 25% (48kt to 60kt) in Q4 FY27 funded by internal accruals, with utilisation at 99% and a ~INR500 crore order book at start of H2 supporting growth, though seamless pipe timing and orders are unquantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects a positive EBITDA margin trend over 3-4 quarters, but Q2 margin only rose to 9.3% from 9.0% and gross margin fell YoY as consumables (10-12% of raw material cost) are unhedged and other costs grew faster than sales.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Melting capacity rise from 48,000 t to 60,000 t (about 25%) is under construction with commissioning guided for Q4 FY27 and funded by internal accruals; solar captive plants are due from 1 Jan 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Utilisation is 99% on billets and rolled products, so volume can only grow with the 60,000 t expansion; management attributed Q2 revenue growth of 33% to richer grade mix rather than volume, and bright bar sits at about 60% utilisation.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation has run at 99% for two years and management is reconsidering the seamless machine order to a higher-output unit, with INR18.57 crore of IPO money still unspent for the seamless vertical.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numeric revenue guidance, but H1 PAT of INR43.9 crore is about 88% of FY26 full-year PAT and the order book is about INR500 crore at start of H2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was only about INR4.5 crore against PAT of INR43.9 crore, receivable days are rising on 60-90 day direct terms, and commissioning of the Q4 FY27 expansion and solar projects could slip.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Seamless pipe B2B bar entry is planned with INR18.57 crore unspent and machinery sourcing delayed, and the 80% year-one utilisation target is not backed by firm commitments.

rows.label: Solar and windmill captive power
rows.why: Solar plants to cover captive power from 1 Jan 2027 and windmills targeted end-March, together covering about 80% of power cost, which should lower power cost and support margins.

rows.label: Free cash flow turns positive for FY27
rows.why: Management says FCF will be positive for the full year, but H1 operating cash flow was only about INR4.5 crore against PAT of INR43.9 crore and receivables are about INR232-242 crore, up from about INR132-137 crore.

rows.label: Seamless pipe export inquiries
rows.why: Management cites a large inquiry pipeline from the Middle East, Europe and US for seamless pipes but did not quantify it, and no firm commitments were stated.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, utilisation and the 60,000 t expansion, but cautious and partial on cash conversion, the unspent IPO money and gross margin, with some figures corrected on the call; analysts pressed on working capital, related-party loans and margin decline.
